alignments.note: Resultative rendering: rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement (`make straight` heads on `straight`), so `make ... perfect` heads on *perfect*. Discontinuous around the object pronoun under rule 15.
Object pronoun of the resultative verb, split off under rule 2.
Preposition realized by *in* under rule 36.
Universal quantifier rendered *every*; no negator stands with it, so rule 87 is not in question.

Substantival adjective expanded with a generic English noun; rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on the adjective. The Greek is anarthrous, so rule 102 (article taking a supplied nominal) does not reach it and rule 51's anarthrous clause makes *thing* an ordinary rule 7 helper on `ἀγαθῷ`.

Preposition governing an articular infinitive takes the English clause-introducer under rule 61; here the ASV writes only the bare infinitival *to*, which is rule 24's habit against the same construction rendered *to the end that*.
Nominalizing article of the articular infinitive, `unrepresented` under rules 61 and 23; the ASV writes no determiner of its own for it.
The infinitive keeps its own verb, the introducing *to* having gone to `εἰς` under rule 61.
Article displaced by the possessive under rule 20: the genitive `αὐτοῦ` is present and free to carry *his*, so the article realizes nothing.
Head noun, bare after rule 20 gave the possessive to the genitive pronoun.
Genitive pronoun realized as the possessive determiner under rule 20; rule 76's availability test is satisfied, the pronoun carrying no other English word here.
Participle rendered by the bare English participle.
Preposition realized by *in* under rule 36.
Dative pronoun. The projection carries the base reading `ἡμῖν` at SBLGNT.HEB.13.21.v008, which the ASV's *in us* matches; the marginal *you* is not this file's decision under rule 12.

Substantival article before an adjective, no head noun expressed: rule 22 gives it *that which*, and rule 77 records that a substantival `τὸ` heads on *that* in all nine corpus units and on the relativizer in none. No participle follows, so rule 32 does not split it.

Adjectival predicate takes the supplied copula under rule 53 (`ὅμοια` → *were like*); giving *is* to the article was the competing reading, but rule 31 hands a copula to the article only where the modifier is a prepositional phrase with no word to carry it. Head on *pleasing* under rule 104: the `εὐ-` compounds head the stem word in all four units of `εὐάρεστος` → *well pleasing*.

Improper preposition keeping the whole English frame that renders the adverb, discontinuous around the possessive under rule 15. Rule 71 settles the head on the frame's lexical noun — `ἐνώπιον` → *in the sight of* heads on *sight* at 2CO.7.12, 2CO.8.21 and the REV run — and rule 95 confirms `ἐνώπιον` is improper despite its PREP tag.
Governed genitive pronoun realized by the possessive inside the frame; no article stands here for rule 21 to hand a case preposition to.
Proper preposition realized by *through*.
Split from `Χριστοῦ` under rules 17 and 26 rather than sharing one head.
Separately recoverable name, split under rule 26.

Verbless clause whose subject is the noun `δόξα`, so rule 63 keeps the supplied copula off the subject and on the predicate; the dative relative is that predicate, and rule 53 gives it the copula as it gives *am in* to a prepositional predicate. The case preposition *to* rides along under rule 21. Head on *whom*, the word realizing the pronoun. Giving the copula to `δόξα` instead is the defensible alternative and is what JUD.1.25, PHP.4.20, REV.5.13 and REV.7.12 do, but in each of those the dative is a noun or an article that rule 21 has already loaded with a determiner and a case preposition, leaving the nominative the only free host; where a bare dative pronoun stands as it does here, GAL.1.5 — the verbatim twin, identical Greek and identical English — with EPH.3.21, 1PE.5.11 and 2PE.3.18 gives it the copula, and REV.1.6 is the lone unit the other way. Rule 53's own cited `ὧν ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν` → *whose glory is in their shame* confirms the analysis: `δόξα` is the subject and takes nothing, the copula going to whatever realizes the predicate.
Article realized by *the* under rule 19; nothing else competes for the determiner slot.
Subject noun, bare after the article took *the* and the predicate took the copula.
Rule 30's duration idiom: the ASV writes *for ever and ever* rather than compressing to *evermore*, so `εἰς` takes *for*.
Neither article of `εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων` has a distinct English realization; rule 30 makes each its own `unrepresented` unit.
First `αἰῶνας` takes *ever* under rule 30.
Second article of the duration idiom, `unrepresented` under rule 30. The projection carries r01 at SBLGNT.HEB.13.21.v009, which supplies `τῶν αἰώνων`; the ASV's *and ever* matches it.
Second `αἰώνων` takes *and ever* under rule 30, the juncture being an obligatory helper on the word it introduces as in rule 29 and not `added`.
Transliterated Hebrew particle rendered *Amen*.

review_notes: Every s### and t### appears exactly once; 30 source and 35 target IDs partitioned.

Four `unrepresented` units, all articles: s007 (articular infinitive, rule 61), s009 (displaced by `αὐτοῦ`, rule 20), s026 and s028 (duration idiom, rule 30). No preposition, particle or content word is left empty.

Heads reviewed separately from edges under rule 28: `make ... perfect` on *perfect* (rule 17), `good thing` on *good* (rule 17), `in his sight` on *sight* (rules 71 and 95), `well pleasing` on *pleasing* (rule 104), `that which` on *that* (rule 77).

The one materially contested unit is s016: *is* could have gone to the substantival article with *that which is*, but rule 31 confines that to a modifier with no verb to carry the copula, and rule 53 gives an adjectival predicate its own copula. Recorded in the note.

s022's copula placement follows rule 63 rather than English word order; the alternative of putting *be* on `δόξα` would make the subject carry it, which rule 63 refuses where the subject is a lexical noun.

Textual notes are not re-decided here under rule 12: v007 and v008 stand on the base and v009 on r01, all compatible with the ASV as printed, and neither margin (*work*, *you*) is FALLBACK EXCLUDED, so rule 97 is not in question.
